records.officialDescription:
Energy Recovery (NASDAQ: ERII) creates technologies that solve complex challenges for industrial fluid-flow markets worldwide. Building on our pressure exchanger technology platform, we design and manufacture solutions that make industrial processes more efficient and sustainable. What began as a game-changing invention for desalination has grown into a global business advancing the environmental sustainability of customers’ operations in multiple industries. Headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, Energy Recovery has manufacturing, research and development facilities across California and Texas with sales and on-site technical support available globally. For more information, please visit www.energyrecovery.com. What You Can Look Forward To:

What You Will Do:
• Support R&D projects (New Technology and New Product) involving fluid machines such as pressure exchangers, centrifugal and reciprocating pumps, turbines, turbochargers etc.

• Develop analytical and CFD models to analyze turbomachinery and fluid machinery designs, suggest ways to optimize designs and predict performance over the full operating envelope.

• Leverage commercial CFD tools such as ANSYS CFX/Fluent and/or STAR-CCM+ to generate computational meshes, perform CFD analyses and postprocess results.

• Build 1-D steady-state and transient fluid system models using tools such as Simscape, GT-SUITE, Simcenter Flomaster or equivalent to analyze and optimize machine and system performance.

• Help develop validation test plans and work closely with testing teams to confirm and validate model predictions. Use commercial and open-source software to process test data and draw physics-based insights and inputs for models.

• Help develop validated semi-empirical performance models of ERI products for use by engineering, sales, and customers.

• Participate in the development cycle of a fluid machine including 1-D hydraulic sizing, engineering analyses, design reviews, experimental validation, RCAs & release to manufacturing.

• Collaborate with multi-national, cross-functional teams across time zones.

• Follow ERI’s structured, phase-gated development process, contributing to design reviews and documentation at each phase.

• Contribute to the development of validated design tools and design practices.

• Other duties and projects as assigned.
What You Bring to the Table:
• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering (or related discipline) with 2+ years of relevant industry experience, or a Master's degree with 1+ years of relevant industry experience, required. Concentration in mechanics of fluids highly desirable.

• Strong background in fluid mechanics and fluid machinery required.

• Hands-on experience in commercial CFD solvers such as ANSYS CFX/Fluent or STAR-CCM+ required.

• Experience with 1-D fluid flow / system modeling tools such as Simscape, GT-SUITE or equivalent is highly desirable.

• Experience modeling turbomachinery such as pumps, turbines, compressors or fans required.

• Experience with product development of fluid machines a plus.

• Familiarity with CAD packages such as SolidWorks/Onshape/Creo/NX/CATIA and programming/scripting (Python, MATLAB) desirable.

• Proficiency in using AI tools to accelerate engineering work (e.g. research, scripting/automation, data analysis, documentation), with sound engineering judgment to verify AI-generated results, is a plus.

• Graduate-level coursework in fluid mechanics, CFD and turbomachinery highly desirable.

• Must possess a demonstrated ability to work in a team environment, manage multiple tasks, and be goal oriented.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Must be willing to work from ERI's India office once it is established; the role will be remote until then.

• Regular overlap with US Pacific time, typically 2-4 hours in the IST evening, in-office workday…

records.title: Intern - Gen AI
records.officialDescription:
ABOUT US
At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers - all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Management Support team works across OakNorth's leadership to keep strategic and operational work running smoothly. The team handles a wide range of responsibilities - from financial tracking and expense management to business research - and is known for being trusted, accurate, and responsive. Much of the team's current tooling runs on Excel, and there's a real appetite to modernise. This is a team that values clear thinking, strong execution, and people who take ownership of making things better.

ABOUT THE ROLE
We're looking for an AI Intern to join the Management Support team in Gurgaon. You'll work hands-on to identify where manual, spreadsheet-based processes can be replaced with smarter, AI-powered tools - and then build them. This role is for someone who's genuinely curious about applied AI, comfortable working independently, and motivated by the tangible impact of turning a clunky spreadsheet into something that actually works.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
• Audit existing Excel-based workflows across the team and identify where automation, AI tools, or improved interfaces would meaningfully reduce manual effort - then design and build those solutions.
• Build and maintain functional tools, dashboards and trackers using Python, VBA, and AI platforms (including Claude, ChatGPT and Notion) that the team can rely on day-to-day.
• Conduct research on internal business questions and external topics - market, industry, or regulatory - and present findings in clear, actionable formats.
• Work closely with team members to understand pain points, translate them into technical requirements, and deliver solutions iteratively with their input.
• Document tools, monitor their usage, and track the time and effort they save - identifying issues early and improving based on real-world use.

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…
• Strong proficiency in Excel and working knowledge of Python and/or VBA - you're comfortable building, not just using.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Collaborate with ML Evaluation Engineers to run benchmark and regression tests.

• Write clean, tested, maintainable Python code and contribute to internal tools, data processing scripts, and annotation/evaluation workflows.

WHAT WE EXPECT

• 1.5-4 years of hands-on experience in ML, NLP, LLMs, or data-intensive software engineering.

• Strong Python programming skills and willingness to work with messy real-world data.

• Familiarity with PyTorch, HuggingFace, embeddings, transformers, RAG, prompt engineering, and basic fine-tuning.

• Good understanding of precision/recall/F1, train/validation/test splits, overfitting, error analysis, and experiment tracking.

• Ability to learn clinical domain concepts and ask clarifying questions about labels and data.

• Strong ownership of assigned modules and tasks.

NICE TO HAVE

• Clinical NLP, biomedical text, healthcare documents, or information extraction experience.

• Experience with LangChain/LlamaIndex, vector databases, spaCy, OCR/document processing, annotation tools, or structured LLM outputs.

• Exposure to Docker, APIs, ML deployment, MLflow/W&B, or data pipelines.

SUCCESS IN 6 MONTHS

• Independently owns modules or bounded workstreams.

• Writes reliable code and experiments with clear documentation.

• Can analyze model errors and suggest meaningful improvements.

• Collaborates well with clinical data, evaluation, and MLOps functions.

About Triomics
Triomics is building the agentic AI layer for oncology EHRs. Cancer hospitals spend billions on highly trained staff manually reading unstructured patient records - pathology reports, clinical notes, genomic panels - to power workflows like trial matching, registry curation, visit prep, and quality reporting. We replace that manual work with task-driven AI agents that sit inside the EMR and process records at scale, in real time.
Our platform is trusted by leading cancer centers including Memorial Sloan Kettering, Mount Sinai, and Yale Cancer Center. We have grown 10x in the last year and process millions of oncology medical documents monthly.

records.title: Offensive Security & Threat Hunting Engineer
records.officialDescription:
ABOUT US 
Glomo builds cross-border payment infrastructure. Our network connects local payment rails across countries, so customers move money across borders in seconds. We are a licensed Payment Service Provider at GIFT IFSC, regulated by IFSCA, and the first of our kind in India. We are also a Visa Principal Member, the first non-bank acquirer in India to join the network, so we acquire and process Visa card payments directly. The team behind Glomo has more than 100 years of combined experience in building large payment products.

YOUR IMPACT
Glomo moves real money across borders and handles card data and customer KYC records. That makes us a target. This role exists to find the ways into our systems before an attacker does, and to catch the ones who get in anyway. You split your time between offence and hunting. On offence, you test our cloud, APIs, networks, and employee endpoints the way a real attacker would. On the hunting side, you work through endpoint, network, and identity logs for what our alerts missed. You work alongside the IT and Infrastructure team and see each finding through to the fix. Your testing also backs our PCI-DSS and regulatory audits.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
Penetration testing. Run regular internal and external tests across our networks, cloud environments, APIs, and employee endpoints to uncover weak points and misconfigurations.
Threat hunting. Dig through endpoint telemetry (EDR), network logs, and identity provider logs for unauthorised access, lateral movement, and anomalies that our automated alerts did not catch.
Adversary simulation and purple teaming. Simulate realistic attacks, including credential theft, phishing, and AI-assisted attacks, then work with our IT and Infrastructure team to close the gaps you find.
Automation. Write scripts and use AI-assisted security tools so that vulnerability discovery and attack surface monitoring run continuously. 
Reporting. Write up each finding so that an engineer can act on it: what you did, what it exposes, and how to fix it, in priority order. No bloated, copy-pasted scanner reports.

WHAT YOU WILL BRING
Experience. 3+ years of hands-on work in penetration testing, red teaming, or threat hunting.
Endpoint and network depth. You know Windows and Linux internals, Active Directory and cloud identity attacks, and how Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools work.
Tooling and scripting. You are comfortable with Burp Suite, Nmap, BloodHound, and Metasploit, you write SIEM and EDR queries, and you script in Python, PowerShell, or Bash.
AI awareness. You know how attackers use AI, for example for automated recon, you can test LLM and API security, and you use automation to scale your own testing.
Practical credentials. Hands-on certifications such as OSCP, CRTO, PNPT, or GCTI matter more to us than a purely theoretical degree.

GOOD TO HAVE

• An active bug bounty profile on HackerOne or Bugcrowd

• Open-source security tools that you built or contribute to

• Security testing in payments or fintech, including PCI-DSS penetration test requirements

• GCP and Kubernetes attack paths

• Detection engineering: turning hunt findings into alert rules

WHY JOIN US
High autonomy
You own how we test, harden, and monitor our entire technical footprint.
Builder culture
Your findings go straight to the engineers who fix them. No endless bureaucracy.

PERKS AND BENEFITS

• Ground-floor opportunity at a fast-growing company, where your work directly sets our direction

• Accelerated career growth: we invest in your development

• Competitive compensation with equity ownership

• Comprehensive health insurance, flexible time off, and a professional development budget

• A close team that celebrates wins and supports each other

**HACK.2027** is the flagship **National-Level 24-Hour Hybrid Hackathon** hosted by **SIMATS Engineering (Saveetha School of Engineering), Chennai**. Designed to bring together 1,000+ student innovators, developers, and problem-solvers from across India, HACK.2027 challenges builders to turn bold ideas into working, real-world prototypes. Students currently enrolled in undergraduate or postgraduate programmes at recognised colleges and universities are welcome to participate, subject to the final eligibility rules. ### Event Format - Mode: Offline - Duration: 24 hours - Team Size: 2–4 participants - Expected Participation: 100–150 students - Location: Chennai, Tamil Nadu ### Our Vision TEXUS 2027 aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and practical innovation by connecting student talent with industry challenges, technological opportunities and collaborative problem-solving. records.title: Makeathon 9.0
records.officialDescription:
Now in its ninth edition, **MAKEATHON 9.0** is the flagship hackathon of the Microsoft Learn Student Chapter. It brings together developers, designers, and problem solvers from across the country to turn ideas into working solutions. Through workshops, mentorship, and a focused 24-hour building experience, participants will explore real-world challenges and demonstrate what they can create together. **Who can participate?** Undergraduate and postgraduate students from all colleges, academic years, and disciplines are welcome. Teams can include students from different colleges and disciplines. A mix of skills in development, design, AI/ML, and databases is encouraged. Each team must choose one problem statement from the officially released list and build a solution that directly addresses it. **Round 1 — Online Screening** Teams must submit: - A project proposal explaining the problem, proposed solution, technical approach, and expected impact. - An implementation plan outlining how the solution will be developed. Submissions will be evaluated on innovation, relevance, feasibility, and clarity. Shortlisted teams will advance to the on-campus hackathon. **Round 2 — On-Campus Hackathon** Shortlisted teams will develop a functional prototype from scratch during the hackathon. Pre-built solutions or prototypes are not permitted, and physical attendance throughout the hackathon is compulsory. Judges will conduct periodic progress checkpoints, followed by a final evaluation. **Final Submission** Each team must provide: - A functional prototype with a live demonstration. - A GitHub repository containing the source code. - A project presentation with at least seven slides. - Project documentation. Final evaluation will consider innovation, technical implementation, practicality, cost efficiency, and overall impact. **Participation Guidelines** - Register through the official platform using accurate participant details. - Work on only one official problem statement. - Submit original work. Plagiarism will result in disqualification. - Demonstrate your own understanding of the project and avoid AI-generated presentation content. - Join the official event community and follow the Code of Conduct. - Violations of event rules may result in disqualification. Judges’ decisions are final and binding. ## Hackathon Resources **(A) [Access Langfuse Coding agent here all free!](https://langfuse.com/)** **Langfuse coupon code:** LF-NONPROFIT-X5MSL **(B) Probe0 setup documentation for Mac:** 1. Open Terminal and run: curl -fsSL https://probe0.xyz/i/h-makeathon | bash 2. Sign in once when asked, and enter the Mac password once. That trusts a local certificate, which is how probe0 sees the agent traffic. 3. Open a new terminal and use Claude Code or Codex as usual. The probe0 dashboard shows what every call used. 4. Nothing leaves the machine, and running probe0 uninstall removes everything. Demo [Link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zrEUf4iqlpyQarQhjkDI-3PLA29mAB2Y/view?usp=sharing) for Probe0 Setup There is also a Mac app download [here](https://probe0.xyz/betaInstall)

records.title: Touch Some Grass
records.officialDescription:
# TOUCH SOME GRASS ### Touch Grass. Touch Hardware. Ship it. We're taking innovation out of the usual coding environment. **TOUCH SOME GRASS** is a Hardware and AI Embedded Systems Hackathon, challenging builders, engineers, designers and innovators to step beyond conventional software development and create solutions that interact with the real world. From intelligent machines and connected devices to AI-powered systems and unconventional hardware innovations, this is where ideas move beyond screens and become something tangible. Forget building just another application. Think about the problems around you. Experiment with technology. Combine hardware, software and intelligence to create something that actually makes a difference. ### WHAT'S THE CHALLENGE? Explore the intersection of hardware, artificial intelligence and real-world problem-solving. Push boundaries, experiment with emerging technologies, and turn ambitious ideas into functional prototypes. Whether you're passionate about robotics, AI/ML, embedded systems, IoT or unconventional engineering, there's room to experiment, innovate and build. ### WHAT TO EXPECT - **Build from Scratch:** Transform ideas into working prototypes. - **Hardware Meets Intelligence:** Explore the possibilities of combining physical systems with AI. - **Experiment Without Limits:** Challenge conventional approaches and explore unconventional solutions. - **Real-World Innovation:** Build technology that extends beyond the screen. - **Showcase Your Creation:** Put your engineering, creativity and problem-solving skills to the test. ### WHO CAN PARTICIPATE? Students, developers, hardware enthusiasts, robotics enthusiasts, AI researchers, designers and anyone passionate about building technology are welcome. You don't need to have everything figured out. You just need an idea, the curiosity to experiment and the willingness to build. ### THE BOTTOM LINE Less scrolling. More building. Step outside the ordinary, get your hands dirty, and make something that exists beyond your laptop. **It's time to TOUCH SOME GRASS.**
